shared_elements: animal shown in profile (horse head in A, quadruped/bird in B)
human or anthropomorphic elements (bearded head and hands in A; arms/hands and hand-like forms in B)
incised linear detailing (mane/hair in A, fur/feather hatching in B)
justification: Both are stone surfaces worked in low relief with profile animals and human/limb motifs, and both are divided by a horizontal band that separates an upper from a lower zone, which is the most specific correspondence. Otherwise they diverge sharply: A is a smooth, naturalistic, tightly modelled panel with careful anatomical and harness detail arranged in a single continuous scene, while B is a coarse, schematic pillar with isolated, flatly outlined creatures scattered over an unpolished block.
